title: Gate execution vs status-read command semantics are misleading
description:
Friction observed while lead-driving epic 2821e177 (2026-07-03).

The gate command names invert their semantics relative to what a reader expects:

- `jit gate check-all <id>` only READS recorded statuses; it does not evaluate anything. Its output for a never-run gate is "Gate 'cargo-ci' has not been run yet for issue <id>. Use 'jit gate pass' to run it." — yet it exits 0. An orchestrator that runs `check-all` expecting gate evaluation (the natural reading, and what the jit-execution-lead skill's review protocol implies with "Run jit gate check-all") gets a silent no-op: all gates still pending, exit code green.
- `jit gate pass <id> <gate>` EXECUTES the checker. The verb "pass" reads as "force-mark this gate passed" (an override), which is the opposite of what it does, and is alarming to type for an agent bound by gates-are-inviolable rules.

## Plan

Design + decisions: `dev/active/949cd9d0-gate-verb-semantics.md`.

Rename the gate verbs so each tells the truth about what it does, additively (legacy names retained as silent aliases here; their removal is deferred to a separate 1.0-milestone-blocking issue):

- Execution verb `evaluate` (short alias `eval`) + batch `evaluate-all`; `pass`/`pass-all` retained as silent aliases.
- Read verb `status` (per-gate) + `status-all` (aggregate); `check`/`check-all` retained as silent aliases.
- `status-all` is strict (single behaviour, no flag): exits nonzero when any required gate — auto or manual — is pending or failed.

## Success Criteria
- [hard] REQ-01: `gate evaluate` (short alias `eval`) executes an auto gate's checker or records a manual gate's attestation identically to today's `gate pass`; `gate evaluate-all` mirrors `gate pass-all`. `pass` and `pass-all` are retained as silent aliases (no behavioural change, no warning).
- [hard] REQ-02: `gate status-all` exits nonzero when any required gate on the issue — automated or manual — is pending or failed, and exits zero only when every required gate is passed. Single behaviour, no flag. Covered by CLI tests for the pending, failed, and all-passed cases.
- [hard] REQ-03: the read surface `check`/`check-all` is renamed to `status`/`status-all`, with `check`/`check-all` retained as silent aliases; singular `status` preserves the existing inspection flags and remains non-strict.
- [hard] REQ-04: subcommand help groups the gate verbs by whether they produce a verdict (mutate) or report state (read), and states which verbs mutate.
- [hard] REQ-05: stale references to the old verbs in live in-tree surfaces are swept — the never-run hint, the `cli.rs` gate-taxonomy doc comments, the top-level usage example, and current product docs under `docs/` — now name `evaluate`/`status`. Out of scope: historical/archived dev docs (`dev/archive`, `dev/sessions`, prior plan documents) and existing issue descriptions in `.jit/`, which are historical records left as-authored.
